data: Polar LEO comms — 66 operational sats +9 spares, GMDSS partner, global voice/data
Iridium NEXT commercial constellation. Replaced the 1998-era Iridium 1 fleet; deployment completed 2019.

Second-generation Iridium constellation — 66 operational satellites at 780 km in 6 polar planes (11 per plane), with 9 on-orbit spares, deployed 2017-2019 to replace the original 1998 Iridium fleet. Total of 75 satellites were launched; 5 additional ground spares were launched in May 2023. Carries voice + data + machine-to-machine + sat-phone services. One of two GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) satellite providers (alongside Inmarsat) — ocean-going vessels can fulfill GMDSS requirements via Iridium OR Inmarsat. The collision of the original Iridium 33 with derelict Cosmos 2251 in 2009 was the first known satellite-to-satellite collision in history.
Largest LEO broadband constellation — over 11,000 active satellites (as of October 2026)
First-gen LEO broadband — 648 sats in 12 polar planes
Only operational MEO commercial broadband — 20+ sats
Europe's civilian GNSS — ~30 sats, sub-metre positioning

66 operational satellites (plus 9 on-orbit spares) at 780 km in 6 polar planes — second-generation replacement of the original 1998 Iridium fleet. Voice, data, machine-to-machine. Backbone of GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System); your sat-phone in a remote ocean runs through this.
